newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel-Palestinian clashes erupt again in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel-Palestinian clashes erupt again in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian protesters threw petrols bombs and rocks at Israeli troops who responded with rubber bullets and teargas in Hebron on Saturday in a second day of fierce clashes in the West Bank city.
Hospital officials said at least 15 Arabs were wounded by rubber bullets along what is becoming a confrontation line dividing the Palestinian and Israeli-controlled areas of the city.

Hundreds of Arab youths shouting "Allahu Akbar" (God is greatest) ran past Palestinian police, who tried but failed to stop them, and hurled petrol bombs and rocks at Israeli soldiers as the violence spread to several Hebron streets, witnesses said.

The clashes were as heavy as those on Friday, when at least 13 Arab youths were injured by rubber bullets and dozens were treated for teargas inhalation in the most serious unrest since Israel handed most of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January.

Tension has been high since Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in occupied West Bank.
On Friday, a Palestinian suicide bomber killed three women in a crowded Tel Aviv cafe. The militant Moslem group Hamas claimed responsibility and Israel closed off the West Bank and Gaza.
The Israeli army declared a curfew on Friday on the Israeli-controlled section of Hebron where 400 Jewish settlers guarded by the army live among thousands of Palestinians.
An army spokesman said the curfew barred Palestinians, not Israelis, from moving around in the area.
